idiom_name: grpc-swift generated service provider/protocol over SwiftNIO (v2: GRPCClient/GRPCChannel)
implementation_notes: grpc-swift generates SwiftProtobuf message types and a service protocol plus a client type: the facade is the type conforming to the generated protocol - its methods take the request message and return the response, using async/await in the SwiftNIO-based generations - and the client is a generated stub bound to a connection (ClientConnection in gRPC Swift 1, GRPCChannel in Swift 2). Swift's value semantics make the payloads natural: messages are structs, so copying them across the boundary cannot leak shared mutable state. The 1.x line is in maintenance mode in favour of gRPC Swift 2, so new code should target the 2.x API; a hand-written Codable/URLSession facade remains justified only for a plain JSON endpoint.
pitfalls: A long-running facade method must not block the event loop: move synchronous work to a NIO thread pool and await it, or every call on that connection stalls.
Response messages larger than the configured maximum receive/send size fail the call; bound coarse responses or stream them.
Generated messages are value types, so a design that relied on the caller observing later mutations of a returned object must be modelled explicitly, for example with a stream.
